Prevention: Use high planting densities (recommended seed rate 80 kg/ha) since sparse planting density encourages aphid infestations.
Encourage intercropping with densely populated maize crop.
Plant 2 bean seeds in between maize stations (25 cm apart) to prevent heavy aphid infestation.
Before planting remove all weeds and and volunteer plants, especially if they are infested with aphids.
Check if surrounding bean farmers are experiencing aphids, or if surrounding bean gardens have aphids.
Use recommended rate of nitrogen fertiliser application (100kg of

Introduce practices that will attract natural enemies such as planting flowering plants around the field, avoid use of broadspectrum pesticides that can reduce the populations of ladybug, green lacewings and birds.
Monitoring: Inspect crops regularly (once or twice a week) during periods of high risk, during continuous dry spells and when crops are about to flower.
Look for colonies of small black/ green soft bodied insects on plants, especially around stems, growing points and undersides of the leaves.
Sooty mould can be seen when there is a high infestation of aphids.
Look for leaf distortion and curling of leaves where aphids have fed.
Affected plants can be slow in growth and struggle to recover, which reduces yield.
Look for ants that may be attracted by the honeydew produced by aphids.
Consider control when 15-20% plants have been infested in the garden.
Direct Control: Uproot and burn nearby dead, infested plants to reduce aphid build up.
